title: Hand-held Clinical Photoacoustic Imaging System for Real-time Non-invasive Small Animal Imaging
protocol: Run the software provided by the manufacturer in the clinical US system.
Select the 'research' button from the touch screen to operate the US system in research mode.
Click on the combined US and PA imaging script from the list of scripts.
Click the run button for imaging in the combined mode.
Synchronize the clinical US system with the laser using the laser trigger out or a photodiode.
Connect the fixed sync out from the laser to the US system sync in.
Provide a positive Transistor-transistor logic (TTL) signal as the sync signal.
Use a photodiode signal for synchronization if applicable.
Connect the photodiode detector to the US system sync in using a photodiode bias module.
Turn on the AC power and switch the key to the left on the laser controller to start the laser.
Ensure the repetition rate is 10 Hz (F10 displayed).
Set the Q-switch delay as low as 170 µs for low laser energy.
Press the select key until you see the delay value, then increase it to 170 µs.
Wait approximately 20 minutes for the laser to warm up.
Open the software interface on a computer and enter the wavelength as 675 nm in the goto menu.
Press the 'start' button to set the wavelength at 675 nm.
Tune the laser from 670 to 2,500 nm but avoid tuning at 670 nm due to instability.
Press the shutter button and turn on the laser using the switch.
Align the laser beam to the fiber input end.
Use a 1 inch (2.5 cm) diameter plano-convex lens of focal length 15 mm to focus the laser beam.
Ensure all light falls on the fiber input end during focusing.
Switch OFF the laser after alignment.
Fit the bifurcated optical fiber into the 3D printed probe holder at a light illumination angle of 15°.
Insert the UST into the center slot of the holder.
Cut the commercially available chicken tissue slab into a 6 x 6 cm² slab.
Using a knife, cut the tissue slab into 0.5 cm thick slices.
Place a point object, like a 23 G needle of diameter 0.6 mm, on top of chicken breast tissue.
Switch ON the laser.
Wear safety goggles when working with the laser for the remainder of the protocol.
Take PA images of the needle at different depths by stacking multiple chicken breast tissue slices of thickness 0.5 cm up to 3 cm.
Apply US gel between chicken breast tissue layers to improve US coupling.
Save and store the beam-formed images as .mat file.
Switch OFF the laser.
Process the data with the in-house code using image processing software.
Determine the axial and lateral resolution by finding the point-spread function from normalized PA signals along respective directions.
Fit the obtained point-spread functions to a Gaussian distribution function.
Obtain the full width at half maximum for each direction.
When imaging very tiny points is difficult, use a slightly larger target instead.
For large targets, obtain an edge spread function.
Calculate the point spread function by taking the first derivative of the edge spread function.
Prepare 6- to 8-week-old healthy female rats for experiments.
Procure NTac:Sprague Dawley rats weighing 220 ± 30 g for studies.
Use female rats due to higher occurrence of breast cancer in this sex.
Anesthetize the rats.
Anesthetize the rat with a cocktail of ketamine, xylazine, and injectable saline at a proportion of 2:1:1.
Add 0.2 mL of the anesthesia solution per 100 g of animal weight to a sterile surgical 1 mL syringe with needle (27G, ½ inch).
Scruff the neck of the rat by hand.
Disinfect the right-lower quadrant of the abdomen with an alcohol swab.
Inject the anesthesia solution into the animal body.
Check for reflex on toe pinch to ensure the animal is anaesthetized.
Remove hair from the region of interest gently with commercially available hair removal cream.
Apply artificial tear ointment to prevent eyes from dryness and accidental laser damage.
Place a blue underpad on the table and position the animal sideways on it.
Administer inhalation anesthesia through a nose cone (0.75% isoflurane along with oxygen at 1.2 L/min).
Clip the pulse oximeter to the hind paw of the rat to monitor heart rate and peripheral oxygen saturation throughout experiments.
Maintain the animal's body temperature using a heating pad approved for animal use.
Apply 0.5 to 1 mL of US gel on the skin using a syringe.
Spread the US gel well using an applicator.
Place a 0.5 cm thick chicken breast tissue slice (6 cm x 6 cm) on the imaging area.
Apply more US gel on the chicken tissue for improved coupling.
Switch on the laser.
Place the handheld probe holder on top of the chicken tissue.
Scan the area by moving the holder right to left in combined US and PA mode.
Set the imaging depth to 2 cm for PA imaging.
Obtain a control image of the region of interest, above the front leg in the thoracic area, before injection of the contrast agent.
Inject 0.2 mL of the contrast agent in the forepaw of the animal.
Massage the injected area well for 2 min.
Scan after 5 min with the handheld probe along the chicken tissue to locate the SLN with the help of the PA signal.
Add 2 more layers of 0.5 cm thick chicken tissue slices on top of the animal one by one.
Locate the SLN to demonstrate the feasibility of depth imaging up to 1.5 cm.
Remove all the chicken tissue slices after imaging.
Switch off the laser.
Place a 0.5 cm thick chicken breast tissue slice on the rat.
Set the wavelength of the laser as 670 nm using the software.
Switch on the laser.
Scan with the probe along the chicken breast tissue to locate the SLN with the help of the PA signal.
Hold the probe stable after identifying the SLN.
Enter the wavelength as 800 nm in the laser software.
Set the speed as 10 nm/s.
Click the 'start' button.
NOTE: This will vary the wavelength from 670 nm to 800 nm at a speed of 10 nm/s.
Set the wavelength to 675 nm for real-time needle tracking using PAI.
Switch on the laser.
Move the probe to locate and identify SLN on screen with the help of the PA signal.
Inject a 23 G needle parallel to the UST through the chicken tissue into the animal to reach the SLN, while guiding it in real-time on the clinical US system monitor.
Turn off the laser after experiments.
Remove the chicken tissue and pulse oximeter from the animal.
Clean the ultrasound gel on the rat with cotton wipes.
Place the animal on its bedding and monitor it until it regains consciousness.
Return the animal to its cage after its behavior is normal.
